newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares succumb to FOMC pressure.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares succumb to FOMC pressure.

text.p: Belgian shares fell prey to growing nervousness about the outcome of the U.S. FOMC meeting on Tuesday with the short-term outlook hinging on whether a rate hike was in the works.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed's policy-setting arm, was due to vote later on Tuesday on whether to tighten interest rates to guard against inflation or leave monetary policy unchanged.
Steady rates would mean a rally to record levels but a rate hike would spell further trouble after FOMC jitters already knocked more than half a percent off the Bel-20 index.

A blend of early losses on Wall Street and dollar and bond weakness further enhanced the uncomfortable feeling in Brussels, which ended 0.55 percent, or 12.30 points, lower at 2,228.00, less than three points above the session low.
A modest 2.3 billion francs worth of Belgian shares changed hands -- with Petrofina accounting for one eighth of total business in value terms.
But the dollar-sensitive oil firm ignored a buy recommendation by brokerage Vermeulen Raemdonck and shed 0.6 percent to close at 12,850 francs.
Non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere and chemicals company Tessenderlo were hit hardest, losing 2.4 and 2.3 percent respectively.

Union Miniere, which closed at 2,880 francs, was troubled by worries that its exchange offer for the rest of its 54 percent owned diamond unit Sibeka could release a flood of shares onto the market and pressure prices.
Tessenderlo, which ended at 17,000, was dogged by some profittaking after last week's rise to record levels following news of a surprise 30 percent rise in Q1 pre-tax profits.
